Updated assessment with Beige Book context: The December 2017 FOMC statement’s moderately positive tone is corroborated by the November Beige Book, which reported modest-to-moderate growth across districts through mid-November, tight labor markets, and notable wage gains in professional, technical, and production roles. Consumer spending was steady in retail with an upbeat holiday sales outlook, while autos were mixed. Hurricane-related rebuilding lifted demand and construction-material costs, suggesting some upstream price pressure, though overall inflation remained contained. Business activity and investment were steady to improving, with some mixed readings in commercial real estate.

Balancing this with the October SLOOS: easier C&I standards support firms’ financing, but tighter terms and softer demand in credit cards and autos, plus weaker demand for some investment-related credit, add a cautious note.

Net effect: Beige Book strength in labor/wages and holiday retail slightly offsets SLOOS headwinds. The stance remains “gradualist” but a touch more positive than the SLOOS-only view.
